en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Ninth Chapter
The Discussion on Past and Future Objects:
Is a consciousness that has a past object without an object? Yes.
Is it not the case that its object is past? Yes.
If its object is past, then indeed you should not say: [that it is present].
“The mind that has a past object is without an object.
That a mind with a past object is without an object is false.
For if it were indeed without an object, then, alas, you should not say so.
“Having the past as its object. It is incorrect to say that what is without an object has the past as its object.
Is a consciousness that has the past as its object without an object?
“Yes.
“But surely, with reference to the past, there is turning back … [and so on] … aspiration?
“Yes.”
If, with reference to the past, there is turning back ... [and so on] ... aspiration, then surely it should not be said:
"A consciousness having the past as its object is without an object.
Is a consciousness having the future as its object without an object?
“Yes.
“Is it not then an object that is future?
“Yes.”
If it has the future as its object, then indeed, it should not be said:
"A consciousness that has the future as its object is without an object.
It is false to say that a consciousness having the future as its object is without an object.
If, on the other hand, it is without an object, then indeed you should not say, "it has a future object.
To say that what is without an object has a future object is false.
Is a consciousness that has the future as its object without an object? Yes.
But is there not, with reference to the future, turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration?
“Yes.
“If there is turning toward, application, and aspiration directed toward the future, then surely you should not say:
‘Consciousness that has the future as its object is without an object.’”
Regarding the present, there is turning toward it …pe… and aspiration; is consciousness having the present as its object "with an object"?
Yes. Regarding the past, there is turning toward it …pe… and aspiration; is consciousness having the past as its object "with an object"?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there turning toward (āvaṭṭanā) with reference to the present? … Is there aspiration (paṇidhi)? Is consciousness having the present as its object possessed of an object (sārammaṇa)?
Yes. It should be admitted.
Regarding the future, there is turning toward it … [and so on] … aspiration; is a consciousness that has the future as its object "without an object"?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Regarding the past, there is turning toward it … [and so on] … aspiration; is a consciousness that has the past as its object "without an object"?
“Yes,” [you reply].
“With respect to the present, there is turning toward … [and] aspiration; is a consciousness that has the present as its object then ‘without an object’?
You should not say so … [and so on].
Regarding the future, there is turning toward it... [and so on] ...there is aspiration; is a consciousness having the future as its object then "without an object"?
Yes. Regarding the present, there is turning toward it... [and so on] ...there is aspiration; is a consciousness having the present as its object then "without an object"?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “consciousness having past and future objects is objectless”?
“Yes.
“But is it not the case that the past and the future do not exist?
“Yes.”
If the past and the future do not exist, then indeed, O sir, you must say:
"A consciousness that has the past and the future as its object is without an object. ... [etc.
... The Discussion on the Past and Future Objects is concluded.
